# Grenat — reference for LLMs

A compiled language for AI agents (`.grn` files): Ruby's syntax, static types, checked effects, built-in agents, prompts, tools, durable workflows. It is NOT Ruby: read this page before writing code; a topic file (index at the end) only when needed.

## Toolchain

`grenat new --app desk` (src/app.grn, src/config.grn, config/models.yml, tests/, db/migrations/), `grenat check [file]` (types, effects, taint: after every edit, fix every error), `grenat test [file]`, `grenat run file.grn args…` (runs `main`), `grenat serve` (routes, webhooks, schedules, job workers), `grenat fmt`.

Errors: E0100 unknown name, E0200 type, E0300 effect not granted, E0310 non-deterministic effect outside a workflow `step`, E0412 untrusted value reaching a sink, E0414 secret reaching a model, E0500 bad declaration. Fix the cause: `.trust!` only a genuinely safe value.

## Differences from Ruby

- Types are written on parameters, returns and struct fields, inferred elsewhere: `def total(items: Array(Item), rate: Float = 0.2) -> Float`. `Int`, `Float`, `Bool`, `String`, `Money`, `Path`, `Email`, `Array(T)`, `Hash(K, V)`, `T?`, `Result(T, E)`, `~T` (untrusted), `Secret`, `Attachment`.
- Optionals, not nil everywhere: `user&.email || "unknown"`. Errors are values: `?` propagates a `Result`; `raise "msg"`, `raise ArgumentError, "msg"`, `begin … rescue KeyError, ArgumentError => e … end` work too (a `def` body may end with `rescue`).
- No `method_missing`, `send`, `eval`, monkey-patching, `require "json"`, gems, `async`/`await`, `attr_accessor` (use a struct field or a `macro`). `require "./file"` only for your own files, at the top level.
- Build a struct by calling its name, `Point(x: 1.0, y: 2.0)`; shorthands `{query:}`, `f(to:, body:)`. `def norm = …` (one line), `def self.load(...)`, `LIMIT = 10`, `GitHub::API` (a module's constant).
- Concurrency, uncolored: `xs.parallel_map(limit: 5) { |x| … }`, `race do … end`.
- Locals cannot be annotated (`x: Int = 1` does not parse); keywords (`until`, `end`, `in`…) cannot be parameter names; no `\` continuation (break after an operator or a comma).
- Not in Grenat: regular expressions (`/…/`, `=~`, `scan`, `match`), `strftime`, `freeze`, `step`, `each_char`, destructuring block parameters (`|(k, v), acc|`: take the pair, `pair[0]`), endless ranges outside an index (`(1..)`).
- Time: an instant is a `Float` (epoch seconds), not an object: `Time.now` (`uses time`), `Time.parse("2026-09-28T08:00:00+02:00")`, `Time.iso(t)`, `Time.date(t)` → `"2026-09-28"`, `Time.today` (a string), `Time.now - 7.days`; no `t.year`, no time zones besides offsets (time topic).
- Ruby's usual string, array and hash methods exist (collections-and-strings topic). Slices count characters, are `String?` / `Array(T)?` (`nil` past the end) and read only: `xs[i] = v` assigns an item, `xs[0, 2] = v` and `s[0] = "x"` are errors (build a new value). `format("%.2f", x)`, `"%05d" % n`, `x.round(2)`.

```ruby
class Counter  # a reference: @ivars need a type or a default
  @count: Int = 0
end

enum Shape
  Circle(radius: Float)
  Rect(w: Float, h: Float)
end

def area(s: Shape) -> Float
  case s
  in Circle(r) then 3.14159 * r * r
  in Rect(w, h) then w * h
  end
end
```

## Effects

I/O is declared, `def main(args: Array(String)) uses llm, env, fs.read("./docs")`; callers cover their callees' (else E0300).

`llm` · `net("api.github.com")` (HTTP, SMTP, IMAP, PostgreSQL to that host: `net("db.acme.io")` for `Db.connect("postgres://…@db.acme.io/app")`; none for SQLite, localhost, a Unix socket, a top-level `database`; `net` alone = any host, when it comes from configuration, `Mail.connect(Credentials.fetch(:smtp, :url))`: a host checked at run time must be granted) · `fs.read("./docs")`, `fs.write("out")` (path prefix) · `shell("git")` (that program) · `ssh("host")` · `db.read`, `db.write` (`db` = both) · `mcp("server")` · `env` (environment, credentials) · `human` (approval) · `time`, `random`.

## Models and prompts

Models are in `config/models.yml` (the first is the default): `fast: {provider: anthropic, name: claude-haiku-4-5}`, `smart: {provider: anthropic, name: claude-opus-5}`; in a single file, `model :fast, provider: :anthropic, name: "claude-haiku-4-5"`. Keys: `openai: {api_key: …}` in `grenat credentials edit`, or the provider's variable (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`…). Providers: anthropic, openai, gemini, mistral, xai, openrouter, groq, deepseek, together, ollama.

A `prompt` is a function a model implements; the answer is validated against its return type (retried if malformed); `##` comments go to the model.

```ruby
enum Sentiment
  Positive
  Neutral
  Negative
end

struct Summary
  title: String  ## 8 words at most
  bullets: Array(String)  ## 3 to 5 key points
  sentiment: Sentiment
end

## Summarizes an article.
prompt summarize(article: String) -> ~Summary using :fast
  system "You are a concise analyst."
  user "Summarize:\n#{article}"
end
```

`user "Extract this invoice.", Pdf.read(path)` sends attachments (documents-and-audio topic).

## Taint: untrusted `~T`

Untrusted: model answers, HTTP bodies, files from the web, webhook payloads, shell output, MCP results, an agent's answer, their fields. Read, print, pass it to a prompt; it may NOT reach a sink — HTTP request, shell argument, file write, email, database write, HTML page, approval text — until cleaned (E0412). A `tool`'s arguments are trusted (the trust boundary): `approve! "Open #{title}?"` is fine there.

```ruby
def digest(text: String) -> Summary uses llm, human
  s = summarize(text)  # ~Summary
  s.check { |x| x.bullets.size.between?(3, 5) }?  # Summary, or the CheckError propagates
  s.check { |x| x.title.size > 0 }.or_else { s.approve(by: :human) }  # a Result, with a fallback
end
```

`x.approve(by: :human)` always shows the value to the human (trusted or not) and returns it trusted, or raises `ApprovalDenied`: review a model's text with `reply.approve(by: :human)`, not by putting it in `approve!`. A JSON field: `res.json["id"].check { |i| i.is_a?(Int) && i > 0 }?`; multi-line: `check do |v| … end?`. Taint follows values into structs and results (json-and-taint topic).

## Tools and agents

A `tool` is a function a model may call, described by its `##` doc and parameter types (its schema: arguments arrive validated).

```ruby
## Reads a documentation page.
tool read_doc(path: String) -> String uses fs.read("./docs")
  raise ArgumentError, "no .. in a path" if path.include?("..")
  File.read("./docs/#{path}")
end

## Opens a ticket in the tracker. Requires human approval.
tool open_ticket(title: String) -> Int uses net("tracker.acme.io"), human
  approve! "Open ticket “#{title}”?"
  Http.post("https://tracker.acme.io/tickets", json: {title:}).status
end
```

An `agent` is an actor; `run` is the loop (model → tools → model…) until the model produces the handler's return type, or `budget`/`max_turns` ends it.

```ruby
struct Answer
  body: String  ## the reply, in the customer's language
  sources: Array(String)  ## pages used
end

agent Support
  model :smart
  tools read_doc, open_ticket
  budget usd: 0.50, time: 2.min
  max_turns 12
  instructions "Answer from the documentation only. Open a ticket for bugs."

  on Ask(question: String) -> ~Answer
    run "Customer question: #{question}"
  end
end

def answer(question: String) -> String uses llm, fs.read("./docs"), net("tracker.acme.io"), human
  spawn(Support).ask(Ask(question:)).check { |a| a.sources.any? }?.body
end
```

A tool refuses an input by raising: the model gets the error (`ArgumentError: no .. in a path`) as the result, the loop goes on (a denied `approve!`: `ApprovalDenied`). Tests may call a tool directly. `run` raises `MaxTurnsExceeded`, `BudgetExceeded`; `within budget(usd: 1.00) do … end` caps spending.

## Workflows, jobs, approvals

A `workflow` journals each `step`: after a crash or a human wait, finished steps are replayed, never re-billed. In a workflow, every `llm`/`net`/`time`/`random`/`human` effect is inside a `step` (E0310).

```ruby
workflow publish(topic: String) uses llm, net("blog.acme.io"), human
  post = step(:draft) { summarize(topic).trust! }
  step(:review) { approve! "Publish “#{post.title}”?" }
  step(:publish) { Http.post("https://blog.acme.io/posts", json: {title: post.title}) }
end
```

A run is its name and arguments: called again with them (after a crash), it replays the finished steps, runs the rest; a key such as `monday: "2026-09-28"` gives one run per period. `enqueue(:weekly, monday: "2026-09-28")` (arguments as in a call; `in: 1.hour`) queues a call for `grenat serve`'s workers; in a job, `approve!` waits for `Approvals.approve(id)` (or `grenat console`).

## Standard library

- `Http.get/post/put/patch/delete(url, query:, headers:, json:, body:, timeout:)` → `status`, `ok?`, `headers`, `body`, `json` (untrusted).
- `Credentials.fetch(:github, :token)` → `Secret`, for every token, password and connection URL (a spec's `GITHUB_TOKEN`; `github: {token: …}` in `grenat credentials edit`): works in HTTP headers/URLs, `Db.connect`, `Mail.connect`, `Ssh.connect`; never printed or sent to a model; missing → `KeyError`. `"Bearer #{token}"` is a `Secret` too, equal to its text.
- `Env.fetch("NAME")`, `Env.fetch("NAME", "default")`, `Env.get("NAME")` (nil when unset), `Env.key?("NAME")`: plain strings, for non-secret settings.
- `File.read(path)`, `File.write(path, text)`, `File.lines(path)`, `Dir.list(dir)` (bare names, not paths); `Json.parse(text)`, `Json.generate(v)`.
- `Shell.run(["git", "status"], timeout: 60, network: false)` (an argument vector, never a shell line) → `status`, `ok?`, `stdout`, `stderr`.
- `Mail.connect(url).send(from:, to: [...], subject:, body:)`. `Db.connect(url)` → `query(sql, [params], as: Row)`, `first`, `execute`, `transaction do … end`; `?` placeholders.

## Serving

```ruby
get "/tickets/:id" do |req|
  id = req.params["id"].check { |i| i.to_i > 0 }?.to_i
  json({id:})
end

on_webhook "/github", secret: Credentials.fetch(:github, :webhook_secret), signature: :github do |req|
  event = req.json.check { |e| e["action"] == "opened" }?
  enqueue(:publish, "pull request")
  "ok"
end

every cron: "0 8 * * MON" do  # UTC; no `uses` at the top level
  enqueue(:publish, "weekly digest")
end
```

A handler's value is the response: a string, a hash/record (JSON), `json(v)`, `html(page)` (escape untrusted with `Html.escape`), `status(201, v)`, `redirect(url)`, an integer status, `nil` (204).

## Tests

Offline, every external call mocked, in `tests/*_test.grn` (or `x_test.grn` with `require "./x"`).

```ruby
test "the agent answers from the docs" do
  mock :smart, replies: [
    call(:read_doc, path: "refunds.md"),  # the model calls a tool…
    {body: "Refunds take 30 days.", sources: ["refunds.md"]},  # …then answers
  ]
  File.write("./docs/refunds.md", "Refunds: 30 days.")
  assert_equal "Refunds take 30 days.", answer("How long for a refund?")
end
```

Doubles: `mock :model, replies: [...]` (each the return type as a hash, enums by name, `{title: "x", sentiment: "Positive"}`; a string; or `call(:tool, args…)`), `mock_http "GET https://api.x.com/*", json: {…}`, `mock_shell "git status*", stdout: "…"`, `mock_env({"SMTP_URL" => "smtp://smtp.test"})` (all `Env` sees), `mock_mail(raise: "SMTP down")` (sending raises `MailError`; `raise: nil` undoes), `with_human(approve_all) do … end` (or `deny_all`; also `.approve(by: :human)`), `freeze_time("2026-09-28T08:00:00Z") do … end`, `request :get, "/tickets/1"` (→ `"status"`, `"body"`, `"headers"`), `deliver_webhook "/github", json: {…}`, `Jobs.perform`, `Mail.deliveries`, `Http.requests`; `freeze_time`, `mock_env`, `mock_mail`, `Http.requests`, `deliver_*` only in a `test`. `assert x`, `assert_equal expected, actual`, `assert_raises TaintError { … }`.

- A `mock` with no reply left fails the test ("mock has no reply left"): that proves a workflow did not call the model again.
- `mock_http` takes `json:`, `body:`, `status:`, `headers:`, `times:`; an unstubbed request raises `HttpError`. `Http.requests` lists what was sent, in order: `Http.requests.last["method"]`, also `"url"`, `"body"`, `"json"` (nil if not JSON), `"headers"` (a secret stays a `Secret`, equal to its text).
- `Mail.deliveries`: hashes, `m["from"]`, `m["to"]` (an array), `m["subject"]`, `m["body"]`.
- Errors: `TaintError`, `CapabilityError`, `SecretError`, `CheckError`, `ApprovalDenied`, `BudgetExceeded`, `MaxTurnsExceeded`, `TimeoutError`, `HttpError`, `MailError`, `KeyError`, `ArgumentError`, `TypeError`, `LlmError`, `RuntimeError` (a bare `raise`).
- In tests `Credentials.fetch(:a, :b)` is the stand-in `"test-a-b"` (`:tracker, :token` → `"test-tracker-token"`), not a URL: to send mail or open a database, `mock_credentials({"smtp" => {"url" => "smtp://u:p@smtp.acme.io:587"}, "github" => {"token" => "t"}})` (replacing all stand-ins).
- Mocked models cost nothing: test `max_turns` (more tool-call replies than turns), not a dollar budget.
- `GRENAT_LOG=1 grenat test …` prints each model, tool and HTTP call.

## Checklist

1. Every function doing I/O has `uses …`; `main` covers everything.
2. Every value from a model, HTTP, a webhook or a tool is `check`ed (or `approve`d) before a sink.
3. Secrets come from `Credentials.fetch`, never into a prompt.
4. Prompts and handlers return typed structs with `##` field docs.
5. `grenat check` passes, then `grenat test`.

## Topics: read `docs/llms/<topic>.md` when the task needs it

- `email-in`: a mailbox read by `on_email`.
- `files-in`: a folder watched by `on_file`.
- `slack-teams`: approvals in Slack, `Slack.post`, Slack/Teams webhooks.
- `rate-limits`: `limit`, `429`, `mock_http times:`.
- `telemetry`: OpenTelemetry (`OTEL_*`).
- `records-and-search`: `database`, records, migrations, `embed`, `nearest`.
- `documents-and-audio`: PDFs, images, audio, `transcribe`, `batch_map`.
- `streaming-and-chat`: `stream` (Server-Sent Events), `Conversation`.
- `agents-advanced`: `tell`, pools, `race`, budgets, `tool_timeout`.
- `workflows`: `return`, step values, jobs, `every`, crash tests.
- `json-and-taint`: JSON fields, `dig`, tainted structs.
- `mcp-and-expose`: MCP servers, `expose`.
- `ssh`: `Ssh.connect`, SFTP.
- `time`: dates, durations.
- `collections-and-strings`: all string, array, hash methods, formats.
